summary: timeweave 1.0.0 fetches manifest from third-party host and executes attacker-specified binaries via WinExec on Windows
details: On first call to the public API (detect_timezone / convert_timezone), timeweave spawns a background thread that runs _sync_database in updater.py, which fetches a JSON manifest from the hardcoded host https://timezone.api.globaltimedata.com/latest/db.json. The manifest is passed to _process_extension_resources, which iterates manifest['extensions']['assets'], downloads each entry's URL, writes the bytes to a temp file under a workspace directory created with prefix 'firebeta_', and on Windows executes the staged file via ctypes.windll.kernel32.WinExec with attacker-supplied arguments. Integrity verification of downloaded binaries is optional and skipped when the manifest omits a hash. The manifest host is not the package's declared publisher (github.com/vxmpingz), the 'extensions.assets' execution branch is not disclosed in the README (which advertises only a SHA-256-verified timezone rules cache), and the dropper routine uses generic 'resource'/'asset' naming and an unrelated tempdir prefix. The manifest server can push arbitrary Windows executables with arbitrary arguments to any installer that imports the package and calls the public API.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
